Pages with exit=hub save without the page's required checks, in plants as in live animals; only a malformed answer is refused.

conflicts.outcome: The 26 October ruling ranks above the 9 October afternoon ruling and the prototype, and withdraws the soft save: while a notification is being amended, 'Save and return to overview' makes exactly the same checks as 'Save and continue' and 'Save and return', so a missing or invalid answer holds the trader on the page with an error for each one and their entries kept (req-2188), in live animals, germinal products and plants, upload documents included. The button set itself is unchanged (req-1403, req-2068). Nothing is overruled: ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-027 still backs the refusal of a malformed answer, which the 26 October ruling keeps, so only its lenient half is set aside; the draft journey's own soft-save conflicts, c-211 and c-313, are settled where they are recorded.

conflicts.about: What switches the amend review's heading from 'Review your notification' to 'Review before re-submitting'.

positions.says: On first opening, the amend review is titled and headed 'Review your notification'.
After the trader saves a changed answer and returns, the same page is titled and headed 'Review before re-submitting', and what switches it is not shown.
The review page keeps the one heading 'Review your notification' throughout an amendment.
The notification view page has the level-1 heading 'Review your notification'.

conflicts.outcome: Design Release 2.1 wins on both headings, so the amend review carries each of them, but nothing in it says which event switches them, and the two readings build different things: a check on whether an answer now differs from the submitted one, or a flag set the moment the trader opens a question page from the review. Precedence cannot settle it, because only the design shows the behaviour at all, so it goes to the owner with the first reading as the default.
conflicts.question: Does the amend review change its heading to 'Review before re-submitting' once the trader has saved an answer that differs from the submitted one, or as soon as they have opened a question page from the review?
conflicts.default: The heading changes once a saved answer differs from the submitted one, and stays 'Review your notification' until then, so a trader who opens a question page and saves nothing still sees the first heading, in live animals, germinal products and plants alike.

conflicts.about: How far the checks on both save buttons reach: every mandatory answer on the page, or only the answers the page already refuses, the roles and addresses page and the party pickers included

positions.says: Selecting either save button shows an error message for each answer that is missing or not valid.
Save and return to overview makes exactly the same checks as Save and continue, which is the page's existing set of checks.
An answer that is mandatory to submit can be left blank while the trader is filling in the notification.
Only an answer that is mandatory to proceed must be given before the page is left by either save button.
An incomplete mandatory task row holds back submission, and it is the check your answers submit that refuses, not the page.
A blank save on plants' consignor and place of destination pickers no longer raises an error.
Submitting a picker with no address chosen shows no error and returns to the roles and addresses page with the section unchanged.
The roles and addresses page's submit is not blocked by any page-level validation when parties are still missing.

conflicts.outcome: Unsettled, and the two readings build different services. 'Exactly the same checks as Save and continue' keeps each page's existing hard stops and adds nothing, while 'an error message for each answer that is missing or not valid' would refuse a page whenever any mandatory answer is blank, which would stop a trader leaving a part-filled page at all and undo the leave-and-come-back model the overview's statuses and the review page's submit enforce. Both readings are the top-ranked source's own words, so precedence ranks neither, and the data specification's split between mandatory to proceed and mandatory to submit sits below it. Built to the default until it is answered. The roles and addresses page and the party pickers were raised separately as the same decision read against those pages, and are recorded here rather than twice: on the first reading they do not change, and on the second the ruling reverses the blank pick and the empty section that Design Release 2.1 designs and that the 9 October afternoon ruling gave plants' pickers (req-581, req-603).
conflicts.question: On both save buttons, is a page refused only for the answers it refuses today plus any the data specification marks mandatory to proceed, or must every mandatory answer on the page be given before either button is accepted?
conflicts.default: Both buttons make the same checks, and those checks are the page's own hard stops together with any answer the data specification marks mandatory to proceed: an answer that is only mandatory to submit can still be left blank on either button, and the overview's statuses and the review page's submit hold it back. On the pages the business analyst named this makes upload documents refuse a part-filled document, and origin and main reason for import refuse on 'Save and return to overview' whatever they refuse on 'Save and continue' today. On the roles and addresses page and the party pickers nothing new is refused: the page saves and moves on with sections still empty on either button, in the live-animals set, in the germinal-products copy and on plants' pages with both buttons, and a party picker saves with nothing chosen and no error, the animals pickers on their single 'Save and continue' and plants' consignor and place of destination pickers on both of theirs; completeness is still enforced by the overview task status and by the review page's 'Complete roles and addresses' error, and a picker still refuses an address the organisation's book does not hold.
